feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $R$ to $Q$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{RQ}=\overset{\to }{RP}+\overset{\to }{PQ},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/c3abc51a0c48faa7853eb2ef605412ca6311866994b15a579b7bc7e7db63ee15.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{RP}=-d,\,\overset{\to }{PQ}=-a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/a53de4a8dcbd4a5d1f7640d5e1d4c8b6fd6e5e24388f432d279392727b11dd59.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{RQ} & =\overset{\to }{RP}+\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =-d+(-a) \\  & =-d-a.\end{aligned}
$$
